question.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{9}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼B(7,\theta )$ and unknown probability of success $\theta .$ For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{9},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{9}{x}_{i}=13.
$$

Find the likelihood function of the sample up to a constant $C.$

*Hint: The probability mass function for a binomial random variable is given by*

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{n-x},\,x=0,1,2,…,n.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=9$ independent binomial random variables with unknown probability of success $\theta $ and $N=7$ trials, for which the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x;\theta )=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{7-x}, & \,x=0,1,2,…,7.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\theta ) \\  & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}}){\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{i}} \\  & =((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{1}}){\theta }^{{x}_{1}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{1}})\cdot ((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{2}}){\theta }^{{x}_{2}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{2}})⋯((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{n}}){\theta }^{{x}_{n}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{n}}) \\  & =C\,{\theta }^{\,\sum {x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{\,\sum (7-{x}_{i})} \\  & =C\,{\theta }^{\,\sum {x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{\,7n-\sum {x}_{i}} \\  & =C\,{\theta }^{S}(1-\theta )^{7n-S}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}})$ is a constant and $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=13$ and $n=9.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =C\,{\theta }^{13}(1-\theta )^{7(9)-13} \\  & =C\,{\theta }^{13}(1-\theta )^{50}.\end{aligned}
$$
